definition: A species that donates a proton ($\ce{H^+}$) to another species.
A species that accepts a proton ($\ce{H^+}$) from another species, using a lone pair to bond to it.
Two species whose formulas differ by exactly one proton, such as $\ce{NH4^+}$ and $\ce{NH3}$; the one with the extra proton is the acid.
A species that can act as either a proton donor or a proton acceptor, such as $\ce{H2O}$ or $\ce{HCO3^-}$.
A base that dissolves in water to give hydroxide ions, $\ce{OH^-(aq)}$, such as sodium hydroxide.
The formation of ions from neutral atoms or molecules, such as hydrogen chloride molecules forming $\ce{H3O^+}$ and $\ce{Cl^-}$ ions in water.
